claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you some questions.

Let me start with: **How many children do you have, and what are their names and ages?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi there! I have one child - Alex, who's 16 years old. I'm wondering if I can still claim Child Benefit for them?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information! You have Alex who is 16 years old.

For children aged 16 or over, you can still qualify for Child Benefit if your child is under 20 and stays in approved education or training.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, studying at school, college, or in approved training programs)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in any education or training at the moment. They left school recently and haven't started anything else yet.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Since Alex is 16 and has left education or training, there is a specific provision that may apply to your situation.

**Has Alex registered with either a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services?** 

If they have, you can apply for Child Benefit to continue for up to 20 weeks after leaving education or training.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, they haven't registered with any careers service or the armed forces. They've just been at home since leaving school.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. Let me ask a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Do you live with Alex in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK and Alex lives here at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just one more question to complete my assessment:

**Has Alex started any paid work? If so, how many hours per week are they working?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex hasn't started any paid work. They're just at home at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on what you've told me:
- Alex is 16 years old
- Alex is not in approved education or training
- Alex has not registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services
- Alex lives with you in the UK
- Alex is not in paid work

According to the Child Benefit rules, for children aged 16 or over, you normally still qualify for Child Benefit if your child is under 20 **and** they stay in approved education or training. 

There is also a provision where you can apply for Child Benefit to continue for 20 weeks if a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training **and** registers with either a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services.

Since Alex is not currently in approved education or training, and has not registered with a careers service or the armed services, you would not be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex under the standard rules.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Assessment Complete**

Unfortunately, you are **not eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex based on your current circumstances.

**The reason:** Once a child turns 16, Child Benefit only continues if they remain in approved education or training (until they turn 20). Since Alex has left school and is not in any approved education or training, the eligibility has ended.

**However, there may be options:**
- If Alex registers with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services, you could apply for Child Benefit to continue for up to 20 weeks
- If Alex enrolls in approved education or training in the future, you would become eligible again and should make a new claim

I hope this helps clarify your situation. If Alex's circumstances change, please don't hesitate to reach out again.
